q: In the workshop programme terminology, the term 'arisings' refers to:

options.A: The scrap arising from jobs in the shops
options.B: The rolling stock becoming due for Periodic Overhaul during a period
options.C: The new machines arising for installation under the M&P Programme
options.D: The staff arising for promotion in the workshop

e: 'Arisings' means the rolling stock that becomes due for Periodic Overhaul during a period; these arisings determine the overhaul load programmed for the workshop.

q: Rolling stock units are 'homed' to a particular workshop, which means that the workshop:

options.B: Stores the unit when it is not in use
options.C: Is the workshop responsible for carrying out the Periodic Overhaul of that unit
options.D: Pays the wages of the crew of the unit

e: A unit is 'homed' to the workshop that is responsible for carrying out its Periodic Overhaul, regardless of where the unit actually runs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before overaged or heavily damaged rolling stock is condemned, it is inspected by a survey committee which recommends whether it should be condemned or repaired.
2. The expenditure incurred on the inspection of stock by a survey committee is charged to the capital cost of the unit.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: a survey committee inspects overaged or heavily damaged stock and recommends condemnation or repair. Statement 2 is false: the inspection cost is not charged to the capital cost of the unit.

q: Where a workshop executes work for an outside body or another Government department on a deposit-work basis, the usual requirement before the work is taken in hand is that:

options.A: The party executes a bank guarantee for double the cost
options.B: The Railway Board issues a special work order for the work
options.C: The party pays only after the work is completed and billed
options.D: The estimated cost of the work, together with departmental charges, is deposited in advance with the Railway

e: For deposit work, the estimated cost of the work together with departmental charges must be deposited in advance with the Railway before the work is taken in hand.

q: The expenditure incurred on the foundation, erection and installation of a new machine purchased for a workshop is:

options.A: Charged to shop on-cost of the shop where the machine is installed
options.B: Treated as part of the capital cost of the machine itself
options.D: Written off to revenue in the year of installation

e: Foundation, erection and installation expenditure forms part of the capital cost of the machine itself, since it is incurred to bring the machine into working condition.

q: Before a manufacture estimate of a railway workshop is sanctioned by the competent authority, it is:

options.A: Vetted by the Workshop Accounts Office as associated finance
options.B: Approved by the stores depot attached to the workshop
options.C: Sent to the Railway Board in all cases
options.D: Certified by the Production Control Organisation alone

e: A manufacture estimate is vetted by the Workshop Accounts Office acting as associated finance before the competent authority sanctions it.

q: Articles manufactured under a batch work order are completed and ready in lots before the entire batch is finished. In such a case, the cost is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense:

options.A: Lot-wise, as and when each lot is completed and transferred to stores
options.B: Only after the last article of the batch is completed
options.C: At the end of the financial year, for the whole batch together
options.D: Only after the batch work order is formally closed by the Railway Board

e: Under batch costing, the cost of each completed lot is transferred out of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense lot-wise as the lot is finished and sent to stores, not on completion of the whole batch.

q: Small quantities of consumable stores required for day-to-day use in a shop are generally held:

options.A: In the personal custody of the chargeman, without any accountal
options.B: In the cash office of the workshop
options.C: Only in the main stores depot, shops not being allowed to hold any stores
options.D: In the shop itself under an imprest arrangement, replenished from the stores depot as the stores are consumed

e: Small consumable stores for day-to-day use are held in the shop under an imprest arrangement and replenished from the stores depot as they are consumed.

q: The annual production programme of a production unit of Indian Railways (the number and type of units to be manufactured during the year) is approved by:

options.B: The General Manager of the production unit alone
options.C: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer of the zonal railway
options.D: The Research Designs and Standards Organisation

e: The annual production programme of a railway production unit, covering the number and type of units to be manufactured, is approved by the Railway Board.

q: In job costing as followed in railway workshops, the 'cost unit' is:

options.A: The individual job or work order, for which cost is separately collected
options.B: One machine hour worked in the shop
options.C: One tonne of material consumed in the workshop
options.D: The shop as a whole for the year

e: In job costing, cost is collected separately for each individual job or work order, which is therefore the cost unit.

q: Adoption of uniform costing principles and methods in all workshops of Indian Railways is useful mainly because it:

options.A: Eliminates the need for maintaining the Workshop General Register
options.B: Fixes the same on-cost percentage for every workshop
options.C: Makes the unit costs of different workshops comparable with each other
options.D: Dispenses with the internal check of labour pay sheets

e: Uniform costing principles make the unit costs of different workshops comparable with each other, enabling inter-workshop cost comparison.

q: The manufacture of a locomotive, whose components are produced by different methods (castings in the foundry, machined parts in the machine shop, final assembly in the erecting shop), is an example of:

options.D: Multiple (composite) costing, combining several costing methods

e: Locomotive manufacture combines several methods - castings, machining and assembly - so it is multiple (composite) costing, not any single method.

q: Patterns for foundry castings are made slightly larger than the finished casting required, in order to provide for:

options.A: The thickness of paint to be applied on the casting
options.B: Shrinkage (contraction) of the metal as it cools and solidifies
options.C: Errors in weighment of the metal charge
options.D: Expansion of the moulding sand when heated

e: Patterns are made larger than the finished casting to allow for shrinkage (contraction) of the metal as it cools and solidifies.

q: In a foundry, 'cores' used for forming the hollow portions of castings are prepared in:

options.D: The machine shop

e: Cores, which form the hollow portions of castings, are prepared in the core shop (core-making section) of the foundry.

q: Processes such as hardening, tempering and annealing of steel components in a workshop are carried out in:

options.D: The wheel shop

e: Hardening, tempering and annealing of steel components are heat-treatment processes carried out in the heat treatment shop.

q: The trimming (upholstery) shop of a carriage workshop is primarily concerned with:

options.D: Furnishing work of coaches, such as cushions, curtains and rexine/leather work

e: The trimming shop does the furnishing work of coaches - cushions, curtains and rexine or leather work.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the maximum period for which an adult worker can ordinarily be required or allowed to work in any one day in a workshop (factory), exclusive of intervals for rest, is:

options.D: 12 hours

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker cannot ordinarily be required to work for more than 9 hours in any one day, exclusive of rest intervals.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the period of work of an adult worker in a factory shall be so arranged that no worker works continuously for more than five hours without an interval for rest of at least:

options.D: Half an hour

e: Periods of work must be arranged so that no worker works continuously for more than five hours without an interval for rest of at least half an hour.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker in a workshop works beyond nine hours in a day or beyond forty-eight hours in a week, he is entitled, in respect of the overtime work, to wages at:

options.B: One and a half times the ordinary rate of wages
options.C: Twice the ordinary rate of wages
options.D: Three times the ordinary rate of wages

e: Overtime work beyond nine hours a day or forty-eight hours a week is payable at twice the ordinary rate of wages under the Factories Act, 1948.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a crèche for the use of children of women workers is required to be provided in a factory in which:

options.B: More than 100 women workers are ordinarily employed
options.C: More than 250 workers of all categories are employed
options.D: More than thirty women workers are ordinarily employed

e: A creche for children of women workers is required where more than thirty women workers are ordinarily employed in the factory.

q: Under Emerson's efficiency (premium bonus) plan, a worker:

options.A: Earns bonus on a graduated scale related to his efficiency, bonus beginning at a prescribed minimum level of efficiency (commonly 66-2/3 per cent)
options.B: Is paid at two different piece rates according as he attains the standard output or not
options.C: Receives 50 per cent of the value of the time saved at all levels of saving
options.D: Is paid no guaranteed time wages

e: Under Emerson's plan, bonus is paid on a graduated scale related to efficiency and begins only at the prescribed minimum efficiency level, commonly 66-2/3 per cent.

q: Under Merrick's multiple piece-rate system, a worker whose efficiency is above 100 per cent of the standard is paid at:

options.B: 110 per cent of the ordinary piece rate
options.C: 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate
options.D: 150 per cent of the ordinary piece rate

e: Under Merrick's multiple piece-rate system, a worker above 100 per cent efficiency is paid at 120 per cent of the ordinary piece rate.

q: In work measurement, a 'policy allowance' is:

options.A: The allowance given for fatigue and personal needs
options.B: The allowance given for small unavoidable delays in the job
options.C: An allowance added to the measured time by a decision of the management, and not arising from work measurement itself
options.D: The allowance given for machines waiting for the operator's attention

e: A policy allowance is added to the measured time by a decision of management; it does not arise out of work measurement itself.

q: In stop-watch time study for fixing allowed times, the job under study is:

options.A: Timed as a whole in a single reading at the end of the shift
options.B: Timed only on the fastest worker available in the shop
options.C: Never divided into parts for timing purposes
options.D: Broken down into elements, and each element is timed separately

e: In stop-watch time study, the job is broken down into elements and each element is timed separately to build up the standard time.

q: The relaxation (fatigue) allowance provided in the allowed time for a job:

options.A: Is a uniform percentage for all jobs in all shops
options.B: Is payable in cash along with the wages of the worker
options.C: Varies with the nature of the work and the working conditions, such as posture, heat and the weights handled
options.D: Is fixed by the Workshop Accounts Office

e: The relaxation (fatigue) allowance varies with the nature of the work and working conditions such as posture, heat and weights handled; it is not a uniform percentage.

q: 'Job evaluation' in an industrial organisation is:

options.A: The evaluation of the performance of the worker holding the job
options.B: A systematic determination of the relative worth of jobs, used in building the wage structure
options.C: The evaluation of the cost of a workshop job in the Workshop General Register
options.D: The inspection of a job after its completion

e: Job evaluation is the systematic determination of the relative worth of jobs in an organisation and is used in building the wage structure.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, wages of workshop staff for a wage period must ordinarily be paid before the expiry of:

options.A: The last day of the same month, in all cases
options.B: The seventh day (tenth day where a thousand or more persons are employed) after the last day of the wage period
options.C: Thirty days after the wage period
options.D: The fifteenth day after the wage period, in all cases

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, wages must be paid before the expiry of the seventh day after the wage period (tenth day where a thousand or more persons are employed).

q: Apprentices engaged in railway workshops under the Apprentices Act, 1961 undergo training in:

options.A: Any trade selected by the workshop without reference to any list
options.B: Only the trade of fitter, in all workshops
options.C: Trades reserved for them by the State Government
options.D: The trades designated (notified) for the purpose under the Act

e: Apprentices under the Apprentices Act, 1961 are trained only in the trades designated (notified) for the purpose under the Act.

q: The process (operation) sheets for a manufacture job, laying down the operations to be performed, the machines to be used and the sequence of work, are prepared by:

options.A: The planning/production engineering office of the workshop
options.C: The stores depot attached to the workshop
options.D: The worker who is to execute the job

e: Process (operation) sheets, laying down operations, machines and sequence of work, are prepared by the planning/production engineering office of the workshop.

q: The cost of service shops of a workshop (such as the tool room and the power house) is brought into the cost of jobs by:

options.A: First apportioning it among the production shops served, whose on-cost is then absorbed on their jobs
options.B: Charging it directly to the first job taken up in the year
options.D: Writing it off to revenue at the end of the year

e: The cost of service shops such as the tool room and power house is first apportioned among the production shops served, and then absorbed on jobs through those shops' on-cost.

q: In workshop costing, the process of charging the on-cost of a shop to the individual jobs done in it is known as:

options.D: Accumulation of on-cost

e: Charging the on-cost of a shop to the individual jobs done in it is called absorption of on-cost.

q: On-cost is absorbed on workshop jobs at predetermined rates, instead of waiting for the actual on-cost of the period, mainly so that:

options.A: The actual on-cost need never be ascertained
options.B: The shops can fix their own rates without any basis
options.C: On-cost can be charged at double the actual amount
options.D: Job costs can be compiled and the outturn transferred promptly, without waiting for the actual indirect expenses of the period to be collected

e: Predetermined on-cost rates are used so that job costs can be compiled and outturn transferred promptly, without waiting for the actual indirect expenses of the period to be collected.

q: Flux (limestone) is added to the charge in a foundry cupola in order to:

options.A: Combine with the impurities and ash in the charge and form slag, which can be removed from the molten metal
options.B: Increase the weight of the castings produced
options.D: Serve as the main fuel for melting the metal

e: Flux (limestone) combines with the impurities and ash in the cupola charge to form slag, which separates from and is removed from the molten metal.

q: The progress of outturn of a workshop against its programme is watched by the Production Control Organisation through:

options.A: The labour pay sheets of the shops
options.C: The Plant Register of the workshop
options.D: Charts (bar/Gantt charts) comparing the programmed outturn with the actual outturn

e: The Production Control Organisation watches outturn against the programme through charts (bar/Gantt charts) comparing programmed outturn with actual outturn.

q: In computing a machine-hour rate for a machine, which of the following is treated as a standing (fixed) charge of the machine?

options.A: Power consumed by the machine while working
options.B: Coolants and lubricants consumed by the machine
options.C: Rent for the floor space occupied by the machine
options.D: Consumable tools used on the machine

e: Rent for the floor space occupied by a machine does not vary with its working, so it is a standing (fixed) charge in the machine-hour rate; power and consumables are running charges.

q: In shops where the work is predominantly manual and machine work is insignificant, on-cost may be absorbed on jobs on the basis of:

options.A: The material cost of the jobs
options.B: The number of articles produced in the shop
options.C: The floor area occupied by each job
options.D: Direct labour hours worked on the jobs (labour-hour rate)

e: Where work is predominantly manual, on-cost is absorbed on jobs on a direct labour-hour basis, using a labour-hour rate.

q: For the purpose of collecting and controlling costs in a workshop, each shop or section of the workshop is treated as a:

options.D: Separate accounting unit rendering its own Account Current

e: For collecting and controlling costs, each shop or section of a workshop is treated as a separate cost centre.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The time of a direct worker in a workshop is charged to on-cost, since he is not engaged on any specific job.
2. The time of an indirect worker, who is engaged on auxiliary services and not on specific jobs, is charged to on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: a direct worker's time is charged directly to the jobs he works on. Statement 2 is true: an indirect worker's time, spent on auxiliary services, is charged to on-cost.

q: A 'bill of materials' (material schedule) prepared for a manufacture job in a workshop shows:

options.A: The wages payable to the workers on the job
options.B: The machines required for the job
options.C: All the materials, with their quantities, required for the execution of the job
options.D: The on-cost percentage applicable to the job

e: A bill of materials (material schedule) lists all the materials, with their quantities, required for executing a manufacture job.

q: Worn-out components of rolling stock are reconditioned in workshops (built up and machined back to size) where this is economical. Such work is known as:

options.D: Standardisation of components

e: Reconditioning worn-out components by building up and machining them back to size, where economical, is known as reclamation of components.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. At the close of the financial year, the balances under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are verified with the jobs actually in progress, so that the balance carried forward represents genuine work-in-progress.
2. Balances under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense are carried forward from year to year without any verification of the jobs in progress.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: at the year end, Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balances are verified with jobs actually in progress so the carry-forward is genuine work-in-progress. Statement 2 is false.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker who has worked for 240 days or more in a calendar year is entitled, in the subsequent year, to leave with wages at the rate of:

options.A: One day for every 10 days worked
options.B: One day for every 20 days worked
options.C: One day for every 30 days worked
options.D: A flat fifteen days, irrespective of the days worked

e: An adult worker who has worked 240 days or more in a calendar year earns leave with wages in the subsequent year at one day for every 20 days worked.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an ambulance room is required to be provided in a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed exceeds:
e: An ambulance room is required in a factory where the number of workers ordinarily employed exceeds 500.

q: In the Bedaux system of wage payment, work is measured in 'points' (B units), where one point represents:

options.A: One minute of work at standard performance, including a proportion for rest
options.B: One hour of work at any pace
options.C: The output of the fastest worker in one hour
options.D: One complete article produced by a worker

e: In the Bedaux system, one point (B unit) represents one minute of work at standard performance, including a proportion for rest.

q: Under Gantt's task and bonus plan of wage payment, a worker is:

options.A: Paid only piece wages, with no guarantee of time wages
options.B: Guaranteed his day (time) wages, and paid a bonus on completing the standard task set for him
options.C: Paid at a lower piece rate when he exceeds the standard output
options.D: Paid bonus only when the whole shop attains its target

e: Under Gantt's task and bonus plan, the worker is guaranteed his day (time) wages and earns a bonus on completing the standard task set for him.

q: Components of a large manufacture job which are produced in different shops of the workshop are executed under:

options.B: Sub-work orders opened under the main work order, their costs being consolidated under the main work order
options.C: A separate sanctioned estimate for each component
options.D: The personal account of the shop incharge

e: Components produced in different shops are executed under sub-work orders opened under the main work order, and their costs are consolidated under the main work order.

q: Before being apportioned to jobs, the shop on-cost of a workshop is first collected:

options.A: Directly in the Balance Sheet of the railway
options.B: Under separate on-cost (standing) work orders maintained for the shop
options.D: Through the contractor's ledger

e: Shop on-cost is first collected under separate on-cost (standing) work orders for the shop before being apportioned to jobs.

q: The outturn of a railway workshop is transferred to Stores, Revenue or Capital at:

options.A: The market price of the article
options.B: Cost plus a fixed percentage of profit
options.C: The purchase price of a similar article in the market
options.D: The cost of production, the workshop working on a no-profit-no-loss basis

e: Workshop outturn is transferred to Stores, Revenue or Capital at the cost of production, the workshop working on a no-profit-no-loss basis.

q: 'Time keeping', as distinct from 'time booking', in a workshop refers to:

options.A: Recording the attendance of workers, i.e., their time of arrival at and departure from the workshop
options.B: Recording the time spent by a worker on each job
options.C: Fixing the allowed time for a job
options.D: Preparing the labour pay sheets of the shop

e: Time keeping records the attendance of workers - their arrival and departure times; recording time spent on each job is time booking.

q: The cost of preparing drawings and designs exclusively for one particular manufacture job is treated as:

options.B: Shop on-cost of the drawing office
options.C: A direct charge on that job
options.D: Proforma on-cost

e: Drawings and designs prepared exclusively for one particular job are a direct charge on that job, not general on-cost.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An allowed time fixed under the incentive scheme is liable to revision when there is a change in the method of working, the machine used or the material worked on.
2. An allowed time once fixed can be cut down by the management at any time merely to step up the output of the shop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is true: allowed time is revisable when the method of working, machine or material changes. Statement 2 is false: it cannot be cut arbitrarily merely to raise output.

q: In computing the machine-hour rate of a machine, the 'running charges' (power, repairs, consumable stores, etc.) are those which:

options.A: Remain constant irrespective of the hours the machine works
options.B: Are charged to the general on-cost of the workshop
options.C: Are borne by the worker operating the machine
options.D: Vary, broadly, with the number of hours the machine is worked

e: Running charges of a machine, such as power, repairs and consumable stores, vary broadly with the number of hours the machine is worked.

q: In workshop parlance, the 'outturn' of a workshop for a period means:

options.A: The total wages paid in the period
options.B: The number of workers on the rolls of the workshop
options.C: The work completed and transferred out of the workshop during the period, expressed in quantity or value
options.D: The balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense at the end of the period

e: The outturn of a workshop for a period is the work completed and transferred out of the workshop during that period, in quantity or value.

q: Articles manufactured in a workshop are transferred to the stores depot for stocking only after they have been:

options.A: Paid for by the stores depot
options.B: Entered in the Plant Register of the workshop
options.D: Inspected and accepted as conforming to the prescribed specifications

e: Manufactured articles are transferred to the stores depot only after they have been inspected and accepted as conforming to the prescribed specifications.

q: The Electric Loco Factory at Madhepura (Bihar) is engaged in the manufacture of:

options.D: High-power electric locomotives of 12,000 HP

e: The Electric Loco Factory at Madhepura manufactures high-power electric locomotives of 12,000 HP.

q: The oldest railway workshop of Indian Railways, established in 1862, is the workshop at:

options.D: Kharagpur

e: The Jamalpur workshop, established in 1862, is the oldest railway workshop of Indian Railways.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Labour charges are debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense through the labour pay sheets.
2. On-cost is debited to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense by apportionment of the on-cost collected for the period.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: labour charges reach Workshop Manufacturing Suspense through the labour pay sheets, and on-cost is debited to it by apportionment of the on-cost collected for the period.

q: Periodic Overhaul of a rolling stock unit differs from ordinary repairs in that in a Periodic Overhaul the unit is:

options.A: Completely dismantled, examined and renewed or repaired so as to restore it to the prescribed standard
options.C: Repaired without being taken out of service
options.D: Attended to only in respect of the part reported defective

e: In a Periodic Overhaul the unit is completely dismantled, examined and renewed or repaired so as to restore it to the prescribed standard, unlike ordinary repairs.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. As the volume of outturn of a workshop increases, the fixed on-cost per unit of outturn decreases.
2. The variable on-cost per unit of outturn remains broadly constant with changes in the volume of outturn.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are true: as outturn volume rises, the fixed on-cost is spread over more units so it falls per unit, while variable on-cost per unit remains broadly constant.

q: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget of a workshop is best described as:

options.A: An outlay (suspense) budget, the expenditure finding final allocation under Capital, Revenue or Stores heads on transfer of the outturn
options.B: A final Demand for Grants of the workshop
options.C: A part of the Stores Budget of the railway
options.D: A budget of the earnings expected from workshop outturn

e: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget is an outlay (suspense) budget; the expenditure finds final allocation under Capital, Revenue or Stores heads when the outturn is transferred.

q: The cost accounts of a workshop are integrated with its financial (Government) accounts, the connecting link between the two being:

options.A: The Stores Ledger kept in the depot
options.B: The Contractor's Ledger of the workshop
options.C: The Traffic Book of the railway
options.D: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books

e: Workshop cost accounts are linked with the financial accounts through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books.

q: Where a worker is put on overtime working, the overtime premium, i.e., the extra amount paid over the normal rate for the overtime hours, is ordinarily charged to:

options.A: The job on which he was working
options.B: The Capital account of the workshop
options.D: The Pension Fund

e: The overtime premium, being the extra over the normal rate and not identifiable with a specific job, is ordinarily charged to shop on-cost.

q: An incentive (premium bonus) scheme differs from a straight piece-rate system of wage payment in that under a premium bonus scheme:

options.A: The worker is guaranteed his time wages and is paid a bonus only for the time saved by him
options.B: No minimum or time wage is guaranteed to the worker
options.C: Payment is made solely according to the number of pieces produced
options.D: Bonus is payable even on work which is rejected

e: Under a premium bonus (incentive) scheme the worker is guaranteed his time wages and is paid bonus only for the time he saves; a straight piece-rate system has no such guarantee.

q: Work study, as applied in workshops, is the combination of two complementary techniques, namely:

options.D: Production planning and quality control

e: Work study combines two complementary techniques: method study, which examines how work is done, and work measurement, which establishes the time it should take.

q: Batch costing, applied to standard components manufactured in lots for stocking in a workshop, is a variant of:

options.D: Marginal costing

e: Batch costing, used for standard components made in lots for stock, is a variant of job costing.

q: Merit rating differs from job evaluation in that merit rating is an assessment of:

options.B: The machine on which the work is done
options.C: The method of doing the work
options.D: The worker, i.e., his efficiency, conduct and performance

e: Merit rating assesses the worker - his efficiency, conduct and performance - whereas job evaluation assesses the job itself.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, first-aid boxes, with the prescribed contents, must be provided and maintained in a factory at the rate of not less than one box for every:

options.D: 300 workers ordinarily employed

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, first-aid boxes with the prescribed contents must be provided at not less than one box for every 150 workers ordinarily employed.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the occupier of a factory in which the number of workers ordinarily employed is as prescribed below is required to employ safety officers:

options.D: 1,000 or more workers

e: Safety officers must be employed in a factory where the number of workers ordinarily employed is 1,000 or more.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the 'occupier' of a factory is the person who:

options.A: Has the ultimate control over the affairs of the factory
options.B: Owns the land on which the factory stands
options.C: Maintains the muster roll of the factory
options.D: Is the senior-most worker of the factory

e: The 'occupier' of a factory is the person who has the ultimate control over the affairs of the factory.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, the periods of work of an adult worker in a factory shall be so arranged that, inclusive of his intervals for rest, they do not spread over more than:

options.D: 12 hours in any day

e: Periods of work, inclusive of intervals for rest, must not spread over more than 10-1/2 hours in any day for an adult worker.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, an adult worker in a factory is ordinarily entitled to a holiday:

options.A: On any day of the week chosen by him
options.B: Only on the days of national festivals
options.C: Once a month on the pay day
options.D: On the first day of every week, unless a substituted holiday is allowed as prescribed

e: An adult worker is ordinarily entitled to a weekly holiday on the first day of every week, unless a substituted holiday is allowed as prescribed.

q: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a wage period fixed for the payment of wages to workshop staff shall not exceed:

options.D: Three months

e: Under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936, a wage period fixed for payment of wages shall not exceed one month.

q: Banaras Locomotive Works, Varanasi, was formerly known as:

options.D: Northern Locomotive Works

e: Banaras Locomotive Works, Varanasi was formerly known as Diesel Locomotive Works.

q: The workshop of South Eastern Railway which is among the largest railway workshops in India is located at:

options.D: Bondamunda

e: The Kharagpur workshop of South Eastern Railway is among the largest railway workshops in India.

q: Where a chargeman is engaged exclusively and full-time in supervising one particular large manufacture job, his pay for the period is treated as:

options.C: A direct charge on that job
options.D: Proforma on-cost

e: A chargeman engaged exclusively and full-time in supervising one particular large job has his pay treated as a direct charge on that job.

q: The allowed time for a job is 20 hours and a worker completes it in 16 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 40. Under the Halsey premium bonus plan (bonus at 50 per cent of the time saved), the bonus payable to him for the job is:

options.D: Rs 80

e: Time saved = 20 - 16 = 4 hours. Halsey bonus = 50 per cent of time saved x rate = 0.5 x 4 x Rs 40 = Rs 80.

q: The allowed time for a job is 20 hours and a worker completes it in 16 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 40. Under the Rowan premium bonus plan, the bonus payable to him for the job is:

options.D: Rs 160

e: Rowan bonus = (time saved / allowed time) x time taken x rate = (4 / 20) x 16 x Rs 40 = Rs 128.

q: The total machine expenses of a machine shop for a period are Rs 1,80,000 and the effective machine hours worked in the period are 6,000. The machine-hour rate of the shop is:

options.D: Rs 36 per machine hour

e: Machine-hour rate = total machine expenses / machine hours = Rs 1,80,000 / 6,000 = Rs 30 per machine hour.

q: The opening balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense of a workshop is Rs 5,00,000. During the year, labour, material and on-cost of Rs 20,00,000 are booked to jobs, and outturn of Rs 22,00,000 is transferred out. The closing balance under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:
e: Closing balance = 5,00,000 + 20,00,000 - 22,00,000 = Rs 3,00,000 under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: The total cost of Periodic Overhaul of 40 coaches in a workshop during a period is Rs 96,00,000. The average cost of Periodic Overhaul per coach is:
e: Average cost per coach = Rs 96,00,000 / 40 coaches = Rs 2,40,000 per coach.

q: The shop on-cost of a shop for a period is Rs 90,000 and the direct wages booked to jobs in the shop during the same period are Rs 3,00,000. The shop on-cost rate, as a percentage of direct wages, is:

options.D: 30 per cent

e: Shop on-cost rate = 90,000 / 3,00,000 x 100 = 30 per cent of direct wages.

q: On-cost absorbed (recovered) on jobs during a period at the predetermined rate is Rs 45,000, while the actual on-cost incurred in the period is Rs 50,000. The amount of under-absorbed on-cost is:
e: Under-absorbed on-cost = actual on-cost - absorbed on-cost = Rs 50,000 - Rs 45,000 = Rs 5,000.

q: The allowed time for a job is 25 hours and a worker completes it in 20 hours. The efficiency of the worker for the job is:

options.D: 125 per cent

e: Efficiency = allowed time / time taken x 100 = 25 / 20 x 100 = 125 per cent.

q: On a workshop job, material of Rs 40,000 and labour of Rs 25,000 are booked, and shop on-cost charged on it is Rs 5,000. Proforma on-cost applicable to the job is Rs 3,000. The total (full) cost of the job is:
e: Total cost = material 40,000 + labour 25,000 + shop on-cost 5,000 + proforma on-cost 3,000 = Rs 73,000; proforma on-cost is included to arrive at the full cost.

q: The total cost of a foundry for a period is Rs 9,00,000 and the weight of good castings produced in the period is 300 tonnes. The cost of castings per tonne is:
e: Cost per tonne = Rs 9,00,000 / 300 tonnes = Rs 3,000 per tonne of good castings.

q: Under the CLW pattern incentive scheme, the allowed time for a job is 10 hours, a worker completes it in 8 hours and his hourly rate of wages is Rs 50. His total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus for time saved) are:

options.D: Rs 600

e: Under the CLW pattern, full wages are paid for the time saved: earnings = 8 x Rs 50 + 2 x Rs 50 = Rs 500.

q: A job is booked with direct wages of Rs 50,000. The shop on-cost rate is 40 per cent of direct wages. The on-cost chargeable to the job is:
e: On-cost chargeable = 40 per cent of direct wages = 0.40 x Rs 50,000 = Rs 20,000.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, where a worker does not avail himself of the whole of the leave with wages due to him in a year, the unavailed leave can be carried forward to the succeeding year, but the total leave so carried forward and added shall not exceed:

options.D: There is no limit on carry forward

e: Under the Factories Act, 1948, unavailed leave with wages may be carried forward to the succeeding year only up to a total of 30 days.

q: The allowed time for a job is 20 hours and a worker completes it in 16 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 40. Under the Rowan premium bonus plan, his total earnings for the job (wages for time taken plus bonus) are:

options.D: Rs 800

e: Rowan plan: wages for time taken = 16 x Rs 40 = Rs 640; bonus = (4 / 20) x 16 x Rs 40 = Rs 128; total earnings = Rs 768.

q: Under the Factories Act, 1948, a notice of periods of work for adult workers, showing the periods within which they may be required to work in the factory, must be:

options.A: Kept in the personal custody of the factory manager
options.B: Displayed conspicuously at a prescribed place in the factory
options.C: Sent to the residence of every worker
options.D: Filed along with the labour pay sheets

e: The notice of periods of work for adult workers must be displayed conspicuously at a prescribed place in the factory.

q: The shop on-cost of a machine shop for a period is Rs 1,20,000 and it is absorbed on jobs on a machine-hour basis. The total machine hours worked in the period are 4,000. A job on which 50 machine hours were spent will be charged with on-cost of:

options.D: Rs 600

e: On-cost rate = Rs 1,20,000 / 4,000 machine hours = Rs 30 per hour; charge for 50 hours = 50 x Rs 30 = Rs 1,500.

q: A machine in a workshop cost Rs 6,00,000. Its estimated working life is 10 years, with no scrap value, and it works 2,000 hours in a year. The depreciation charge per machine hour, as an element of the machine-hour rate, is:

options.D: Rs 25

e: Annual depreciation = Rs 6,00,000 / 10 years = Rs 60,000; per machine hour = 60,000 / 2,000 hours = Rs 30.

q: Under Gantt's task and bonus plan, the allowed time for a job is 10 hours and a worker completes it in exactly 10 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 40 and the bonus under the plan is 25 per cent of the time wages. His total earnings for the job are:

options.D: Rs 500

e: Completing the task in the allowed time earns the Gantt bonus: earnings = 10 x Rs 40 + 25 per cent of Rs 400 = Rs 400 + Rs 100 = Rs 500.

q: Under the Bedaux point system, the standard output for a job is fixed at 600 points (B units), representing 10 standard hours of work. A worker completes the job in 8 hours. His hourly rate of wages is Rs 60 and the bonus payable is 75 per cent of the value of the time saved. His total earnings for the job are:

options.D: Rs 660

e: Time saved = 10 - 8 = 2 hours. Wages = 8 x Rs 60 = Rs 480; bonus = 75 per cent x 2 x Rs 60 = Rs 90; total = Rs 570.

q: The normal time for a job, as determined by time study, is 10 hours. Allowances (for fatigue, contingencies, etc.) are provided at 20 per cent of the normal time. The allowed time for the job is:

options.D: 12.5 hours

e: Allowed time = normal time + 20 per cent allowances = 10 + 2 = 12 hours.

q: A workshop worker is paid wages at Rs 50 per hour. During a week, he remained idle for 12 hours on account of a power failure in the shop. The cost of the idle time for the week is:

options.D: Rs 700

e: Idle time cost = idle hours x hourly wage = 12 x Rs 50 = Rs 600, the wages paid for the unproductive hours lost through power failure.

q: The standing (fixed) charges of a machine shop for a period are Rs 90,000 and the effective machine hours worked are 3,000. The running charges of the machines average Rs 20 per machine hour. The machine-hour rate of the shop is:

options.D: Rs 20

e: Machine-hour rate = standing charges per hour + running charges = 90,000 / 3,000 + Rs 20 = Rs 30 + Rs 20 = Rs 50.

q: In a workshop foundry, 200 tonnes of metal were melted and charged into the cupola during a period, and the weight of good castings produced was 150 tonnes. The yield of the foundry for the period is:

options.D: 75 per cent

e: Yield = good castings / metal melted x 100 = 150 / 200 x 100 = 75 per cent.

q: On-cost in a shop is absorbed on jobs at a rate of Rs 25 per direct labour hour. A job on which 240 direct labour hours were booked will be charged with on-cost of:
e: On-cost charged = direct labour hours x rate = 240 x Rs 25 = Rs 6,000.

q: In costing terminology, 'scrap' is distinguished from 'waste' in that:

options.A: Scrap has a realisable (sale) value, whereas waste, such as loss by evaporation or shrinkage, has no value
options.B: Waste has a sale value, whereas scrap has no value
options.C: Scrap and waste mean one and the same thing
options.D: Scrap is a finished product, whereas waste is a raw material

e: Scrap is the residue of materials that has a realisable (sale) value, whereas waste, such as loss by evaporation or shrinkage, has no value.
